subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Titanic: Unsinkable by Design, Sunk by Reality
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Titanic: Unsinkable by Design, Sunk by Reality.

hook.text: The Titanic had 16 watertight compartments. It could float with 4 flooded. The iceberg opened 5.

buildup.text: The ship's hull used brittle iron rivets. In the freezing North Atlantic, they shattered on impact instead of bending.

discovery.text: Watertight compartments didn't reach the ceiling. Water poured over the top of each wall into the next compartment.

twist.text: Only 20 lifeboats were aboard — enough for 1,178 of 2,224 passengers. Regulations hadn't kept up with ship sizes.

climax.text: SOLAS regulations followed — mandating enough lifeboats, 24-hour radio watch, and ice patrol in the North Atlantic.

punchline.text: Designed to survive four breaches. Hit with five. Margins matter.

quiz.question: Why did the Titanic's watertight compartments fail to prevent sinking?
options: The iceberg punctured the bottom of the ship below the compartments
The compartments didn't reach the ceiling, allowing water to spill over into the next one
The watertight doors malfunctioned and couldn't close in time
